subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
title: Platform Bans and Deplatforming
description: A 60-second lesson on Platform Bans and Deplatforming.

hook.text: When Twitter banned a sitting US president, the world debated: should platforms have that power?

buildup.text: Deplatforming removes accounts that violate terms of service. It's effective at reducing harmful content spread.

discovery.text: Research showed that banning prominent accounts reduced misinformation in their networks by over 70%.

twist.text: But banning decisions are made by companies, not courts. There's no due process or right of appeal.

climax.text: Deplatforming works. But giving unelected companies the power to silence anyone raises deep questions.

punchline.text: Effective but unaccountable. Who guards the guard?

quiz.question: What does research show about the effectiveness of deplatforming?
options: It significantly reduces the spread of misinformation from banned accounts
It has no measurable effect on content spread
Banned users always return with more followers
